title: What an extra $200 a month takes off a mortgage
variant: A chart with the whole table under it, and the arithmetic exact
prompt: How much difference does paying a bit more off the mortgage each month actually make?
note: The one with a library, and a demonstration of what the load rule costs: Chart.js draws two balance curves, and the identical numbers sit in a table under it at every anniversary, always rendered. Pull the network and the page loses a picture and no facts. It is also the case for a tool over a sentence -- the answer is non-linear, so the first $50 a month is worth several times the fifth $50, and the only way to feel that is to drag the slider. The opening answer is written into the HTML as static markup and the script replaces it with the same figures on load, so a reader with scripts off, or printing, or reading it in a mail client, still gets the four and a half years and the $52,842. The exact arithmetic is stated as exact, with the four assumptions it is exact under named right beside it, and the last one is that the page has no opinion on whether paying down a loan beats the alternative.
